cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Truth or Loyalty
cards.instruction: Make someone choose between protecting the relationship and answering a dangerous question honestly.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Mum's asking who broke her vase. Will you tell her, or keep your promise to your little brother?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She's blaming the cleaner. I can't let that happen.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Clear the cleaner. Do you have to name me?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She's asked me directly whether you did it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then are you answering her, or keeping the promise I trusted you with?

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 and A5 force loyalty against truth, but A3 asks whether naming is necessary without clearly sustaining the prefixed highest-status role.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 cleaner blame produces A3 limited truth proposal; B4 direct question produces A5 explicit loyalty choice.

relationship.evidence: B2 has an ethical reason to tell and B4 shows why the middle path is unavailable.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4 direct question to make the relationship cost unavoidable.

specificity.evidence: A1 broken vase and little brother, B2 cleaner, establish the conflict concretely.

brevityWit.evidence: A3 question-details phrase is stiff beside the otherwise direct family plea.
